Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed mass with sharp margins in the right hemithorax. This smooth, non-infiltrative border is a characteristic radiographic feature of pleuropulmonary synovial sarcoma, helping to distinguish it from primary lung carcinomas which typically present with irregular, spiculated, or ill-defined borders.
